topics.title: Usefulness of Earthworms to Farmers Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Agriculture
topics.content:
AGRICULTURE
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
THIRD TERM
WEEK 5
PRIMARY 2
THEME - PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS
PREVIOUS LESSON - Diagram of Earthworm Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Agriculture
TOPIC - EARTHWORM
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Identification and Description of Earthworms
2. The Usefulness of Earthworms
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. identify earthworm.
2. State the usefulness of earthworms to the soil.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can describe earthworms.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of chart showing the usefulness of earthworms.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Display chart showing good soil and crops that grow well for the pupils to describe.
Pupil’s Activities - This is black soil and the crops grow well.
Teacher’s Remark - Correct, earthworms enriched the soil to make crops grow well. Ask the pupils to describe earthworms and discuss their usefulness.
USEFULNESS OF EARTHWORM
Earthworms live in the soil and improve soil by their activities.
1. Earthworms allowed air and water get into the soil.
2. Earthworms dissolved the leaves and grass.
3. Earthworms enrich soil by dragging down dead leaves with the soil.
4. Earthworms make the plants to grow well.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Displays live earthworm and sketch.
Pupil’s Activities - Observe and identify earthworm.
3. Discusses why earthworm is called farmers friend.
Pupil’s Activities - State the reasons why earthworms are farmer’s friends.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Usefulness of Earth Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Agriculture
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. describe and draw an earthworm.
2. explain that earthworms live in the soil and improve soil by their activities.
3. state 2 usefulness of earthworms.

topics.title: Methods of Controlling Farmers Enemies | Workbook Assessment Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Agriculture
topics.content:
AGRICULTURE
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
THIRD TERM
WEEK 8
PRIMARY 2
THEME - PROTECTION ISSUES IN AGRICULTURE
PREVIOUS LESSON - Damages caused by Farmer’s Enemies - Rodents, Birds and Crabs Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Agriculture
TOPIC - FARMER’S ENEMIES
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Ways of Controlling Farmer’s Enemies
3. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. identify rats, squirrels, grass cutters, birds and crabs as farmers enemies.
2. State the damages caused by the animals.
3. List methods of controlling them.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify trap, catapult, etc.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Charts or posters of squirrels, rats, grass cutter, birds, crabs, etc.
2. Sample or chart showing catapult, trap, plastic container, air tight cover.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Displays sample or charts showing trap, catapult, etc. for the pupils to identify and state the uses.
Pupil’s Activities - This is trap. It is used for catching rats.
Teacher’s remarks - Correct. Trap, catapult, etc. are used to control farmer’s enemies.
METHODS OF CONTROLLING FARMER’S ENEMIES
1. Shooting using gun and bow.
2. Trapping using cage.
3. Scare - crow
4. Poison
5. Proper storage
DRAW AND LABEL FARMER’S ENEMIES
Guide the pupils to draw and colour rat, bird and crap.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Discusses control method of farmer’s enemies.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate in the class discussion.
3. Teacher’s/Pupil’s Activities - Draws and labels rodent, bird and crab.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to mention 3 methods of controlling farmer’s enemies.
WORKBOOK
Weekly Assessment (Test)
1. __________ can be used to catch farmer’s enemies death or alive.
A. Trap
B. Cage
C. Gun
2. __________ can be used to kill farmer’s enemies by shooting.
A. Gun
B. Catapult
C. Knife
3. If farmer’s enemies eat poison, they will __________.
A. live
B. death
C. strong
4. __________ is used to scare farmer’s enemies away.
A. Scarecrow
B. Trap
C. Net
5. Trap, catapult, gun, poison, etc. are used for __________.
A. controlling farmer’s enemies
B. scaring farmer’s enemies
C. protecting farmer’s enemies

topics.title: Damages caused by Farmer’s Enemies - Rodents, Birds and Crabs Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Agriculture
topics.content:
AGRICULTURE
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
THIRD TERM
WEEK 7
PRIMARY 2
THEME - PROTECTION ISSUES IN AGRICULTURE
PREVIOUS LESSON - Meaning of Farmer’s Enemies | Description of Rodents, Birds and Crabs Primary 3 (Basic 3) - Agriculture
TOPIC - FARMER’S ENEMIES
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Damages Caused by Farmer’s Enemies
3. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. identify rats, squirrels, grass cutters, birds and crabs as farmers enemies.
2. State the damages caused by the animals.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can describe damages caused by farmer’s enemies.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of chart showing damages caused by farmer’s enemies.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Display samples of crops and charts showing plants destroyed by animals for the pupils to examine, describe and mention likely animals that eat the crops or plants.
Pupil’s Activities - The yam is eaten by goat, etc
Teacher’s remarks - Correct. Farmer’s enemies eaten crops. Discuss the damages caused by the animals mentioned by the pupils and note them on the board.
DAMAGES CAUSED BY FARMER’S ENEMIES
Rodents, birds, snakes, crabs, etc. are farmer’s enemies and,
1. They cut roots of crops, for example crabs and other animals.
2. They destroy the harvest, for example rodents (rats).
3. They eat crops and animals, for example domestic (herdsmen) and wild animals.
4. They are harmful to farmers, for example snakes and wild animals.
5. Rats and crops destroy stored stored shrimps and fishes.
6. They bore hole in the stem.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Displays charts or posters of rodents, birds, squirrels, grass-cutters, rats, and crabs.
Pupil’s Activities - Observe and identify rodents, bird and crab.
3. Discusses why they are called farmers’ enemies.
Pupil’s Activities - Describe the type of damage caused by the farmers’ enemies.
4. Summary the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Methods of Controlling Farmers Enemies | Workbook Assessment Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Agriculture
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
state 3 damaged caused by farmer’s friends.
WORKBOOK
Weekly Assessment (Test)
1. Rodents, birds, crabs, etc. are __________.
A. farmer’s enemies
B. farmer’s friends
C. farmer’s companion
2. __________ bored hole in the stem.
A. Goat
B. Grasshopper
C. Bird
3. Crabs, snake and lion eat __________.
A. crops
B. leaves
C. animals
4. __________ destroy stored shrimps and fishes.
A. Rats
B. Goats
C. Dogs
5. __________ cut roots of Crops.
A. farmer’s enemies
B. farmer’s friends
C. farmer’s companion

topics.title: Parts of a Plant | Diagram of a Plant | Workbook Assessment Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Agriculture
topics.content:
AGRICULTURE
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
THIRD TERM
WEEK 9
PRIMARY 1
THEME - BASIC CONCEPTS OF AGRICULTURE
PREVIOUS LESSON - Methods of Controlling Farmers Enemies | Workbook Assessment Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Agriculture
TOPIC - PLANTS
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Common Crop Plants Around
3. Parts of a Plant
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. Name parts of a plant.
3. Draw or sketch a plant.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify come plants like maize and yam.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Freshly up-rooted crop plant specimen e.g. Maize, mango, pawpaw, etc.
2. Chart of well labeled crop plant.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Take the pupils for a walk with the school compound to identify different plants (flowers and crops).
Pupil’s Activities - This is flower, mango tree, grass, maize, etc.
Teacher’s remark - Correct. Plants are crops, flowers and grasses that grown in the soil. Uproot two different plants (fresh) for the pupils to examine (observe) and identify different parts of a plant.
Helps the pupils identify common parts of plants and note on the board.
PARTS OF A PLANT
The main parts of a plant include:
1. Fruit
2. Leaf
3. Flower
4. Stem
5. Root
LESSON 2 - DRAW AND LABEL PARTS OF A LEAF
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Takes pupils round the school compound.
Pupil’s Activities - Observe plants around the school compound.
3. Helps them identify some plants and name their parts.
Pupil’s Activities - Name some plants and identify their parts.
4. Displays chart showing parts of a plant.
Pupil’s Activities - Draw and label parts of a plant.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Parts of a Leaf | Workbook Assessment Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Agriculture
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. Identify parts of any plant.
2. Draw and label any plant.
WORKBOOK
Weekly Assessment (Test)
QUESTION 1
Label each part of the plant below -
QUESTION 2
Draw and label parts of a plant in question 1.

topics.title: Uses of Leaves Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Agriculture
topics.content:
AGRICULTURE
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
THIRD TERM
WEEK 11
PRIMARY 2
THEME - BASIC CONCEPTS OF AGRICULTURE
PREVIOUS LESSON - Parts of a Leaf | Workbook Assessment Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Agriculture
TOPIC - LEAF
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Uses of Leaves
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. identify and name parts of a leaf.
2. draw and label a leaf.
3. state the uses of leaves.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can state the uses of leaves.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of chart showing different uses of leaves.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Get a sample of vegetable soup, pop and moi moi wrap in leaves, etc. for to identify the important uses of leaves.
Pupil’s Activities - Leaves are used for cooking soups, making moi moi and pop, etc.
Teacher’s remark - Correct. Leaves are important to people and animals. They are used for different purposes. Discuss the uses of leaves with them and write on the board.
USES OF LEAVES
1. It is used as food for man. For example, for making vegetable soup.
2. It is used as food for animals.
3. It is used as medicine.
4. It is used for packaging cola.
5. It is used for wrapping pop, moi moi and ekuru before cooking.
6. It is sold for money.
7. It is used for traditional coronation.
8. It is used for serving ofada/selling rice.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Discuss the uses of leaves.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate in the class discussion.
3. Summary the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy the note as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Third Term Examination Agriculture Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Exam Questions
LESSON EVALUATION/WEEKLY ASSESSMENT
Ask pupils to mention 4 uses of leaves.
